【 HK$200 Cash Voucher Lucky Draw】Caregivers Invited to Help Design a Preemptive Social Communication Program 【🎁 港幣200元現金券抽獎】誠邀照顧者參與幼兒早期社交溝通支援課程設計研究 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: QI Xin
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cynthiaqi@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

誠邀家長及照顧者參加研究，分享意見
，
一起設計更貼近家庭需要的幼兒早期支援課程

你是否對孩子的社交溝通
發展
有些擔心？

你是否想參加親子成長課程，卻不確定課程是否適合自己和孩子？
香港中文大學腦與認知研究所正在設計一個幼兒早期親子互動及社交溝通課程。我們希望聽聽家長和照顧者的需要、想法和顧慮，讓課程內容和安排更切合家庭的實際情況。

網上問卷
：
約需15至20分鐘，可使用手機完成

招募對象
18個月或以下幼兒的家長或主要照顧者。
如你符合以下至少一項情況，我們尤其希望聽到你的意見：
你或專業人士對孩子的發展有所擔心
孩子出生時胎齡少於32週
孩子有自閉症家族史
孩子的發展或自閉症相關篩查結果顯示需要進一步關注

點擊連結或掃碼，即可填寫問卷：
https://redcap.link/ugx84w0m

符合參加資格並完成問卷，即可參加港幣200元現金券抽獎
認識可能合資格的照顧者嗎？歡迎把這則招募轉發給他們，謝謝！

WhatsApp
或電話：
+ 852 5589 9581

電郵：
autism@cuhk.edu.hk

Caregivers are invited to take part in our study and share their views
.
Help us design a preemptive support program that better meets the needs of families

Are you concerned about your child’s social communication development?

Are you interested in a caregiver-child program but unsure whether it would suit your
needs
?
The Brain and Mind Institute at CUHK is developing a caregiver-implemented preemptive social communication program for toddlers. We invite caregivers to share their needs, views and concerns. Your feedback will help shape the program and ensure that it better meets the needs of children and families.

Online questionnaire:
takes about 15 to 20 minutes, can be completed on a mobile phone

Who may be eligible?
Caregivers of a child aged 18 months or younger
We would particularly like to hear from caregivers if at least one of the following applies:
A caregiver or professional has concerns about the child’s development
The child was born before 32 weeks of gestation
The child has a family history of autism
A developmental or autism screening result indicates that further follow-up may be needed

Click the link
or scan the QR code
below to complete the questionnaire:
https://redcap.link/ugx84w0m
 Eligible participants who complete the questionnaire will be entered into a lucky draw for a HK$200 cash voucher.
If you know a caregiver who may be eligible, please feel free to forward this recruitment poster to them. Thank you!

WhatsApp or telephone: +852 5589 9581

Email:
autism@cuhk.edu.hk

Midday Oasis: CUHK Christian Band Concert   「午間心靈綠洲」: 中文大學基督徒樂隊音樂會 - Chaplain's Office, Chung Chi College
From: Chaplain's Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chaplaincy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀大家出席即將舉行的Midday Oasis。
今次想為大家介紹中文大學基督徒樂隊。
他們今次一行五人，會帶來不同風格的基督教音樂，同大家分享信仰裡不同的面向——
有輕快的，有沉靜的，有問自己是誰的，也有慢慢願意走出來的。
曲風不一，卻都是他們真心想唱給人聽的歌。
他們希望，音樂可以成為一道門。除了讓人慢慢認識這個信仰，也希望在這個不太平靜的世界裡，大家可以坐下來，聽聽年輕人的聲音，讓心靈有一刻安放。
就算你未曾接觸過這個信仰，又或者只是午間路過，也歡迎來聽一聽。
You are warmly invited to the coming Midday Oasis.
This time, I would like to introduce the CUHK Christian Band.
Five of them will be with us. They will bring Christian music of many different styles and share different sides of the faith — some light, some quiet, some asking who we are, some slowly willing to step out.
The styles differ, but each song is one they truly want to sing for others.
They hope music can be a door. Beyond coming to know this faith, they also hope that, in a world that is not always calm, we might sit for a while, listen to the voices of young people, and let the heart rest.
Even if you have never come across this faith, or are only passing by at midday, you are welcome to come and listen.

A well-designed figure or table can make your research easier to understand, more engaging, and more impactful. Join our Scientific Writing Workshops, co-organized by the CUHK Library and The Independent Learning Centre (ILC), to learn practical strategies for creating effective visual elements for theses, research publications, and conference presentations.
Led by
Dr Sarah E. Webb
, an experienced scientific writer and editor, the workshops will cover:
Designing effective figures, graphs, and tables
Presenting scientific information clearly and professionally
Enhancing the readability and impact of research outputs
Creating publication-ready visuals using professional design approaches
These workshops are specially designed for postgraduate students from
the Faculty of Medicine and the Faculty of Science
who wish to strengthen their scientific communication skills and showcase their research more effectively.
Register now and take your scientific communication skills to the next level!

A well-designed figure or table can make your research easier to understand, more engaging, and more impactful. Join our Scientific Writing Workshops, co-organized by the CUHK Library and The Independent Learning Centre (ILC), to learn practical strategies for creating effective visual elements for theses, research publications, and conference presentations.
Led by
Dr Sarah E. Webb
, an experienced scientific writer and editor, the workshops will cover:
Designing effective figures, graphs, and tables
Presenting scientific information clearly and professionally
Enhancing the readability and impact of research outputs
Creating publication-ready visuals using professional design approaches
These workshops are specially designed for postgraduate students from
the Faculty of Medicine and the Faculty of Science
who wish to strengthen their scientific communication skills and showcase their research more effectively.

各位︰
「嶺南文化與世界」公開講座系列2026──藝文嶺南：工藝、詩畫與人文景觀，由香港中文大學中國文化研究所嶺南文化研究計劃與香港公共圖書館聯合主辦，兩場知識與美學兼具的專題講座將於10 月 25 日（日）及11 月 28 日（六）在香港中央圖書館演講廳舉行。
兩場專題講座聚焦嶺南在跨域交流中的文化生產與藝術創造，從清代廣州工藝實踐與嶺南羅浮人文地景兩個主題切入。一方面，探討廣東銅胎琺瑯器如何在中外貿易背景下融合西洋裝飾元素，體現廣州工匠對外來技術與審美的創新轉化；另一方面，考察蘇軾嶺南詩文對地方知識、人文景觀與文化記憶的建構作用，以及清代與之相關的《羅浮香影圖》。透過工藝、詩畫與人文景觀的視角進行觀察，本系列將展現嶺南文化在跨域和歷史互動中的創新活力。
本講座系列為香港研究資助局協作研究計劃「嶺南文化與世界」項目（2023–2026）活動，亦是弘揚中華文化系列的活動之一。

2023
–2026）
Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries, features two insightful talks exploring the aesthetic side of Lingnan.  Two lectures will be held at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 25 October (Sunday) and 28 November (Saturday).
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

2027/28 Admissions Event: "Meet and Greet" Thursday with DSCCC (29 Oct 2026) 崇基學院2027/28年度招生活動：週四見面會 (10月29日) - Divinity School of Chung Chi College
From: Divinity School of Chung Chi College
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
events@theology.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
崇基學院2027/28年度招生活動：「Meet and Greet」週四見面會 (10月29日)
秋意漸濃，不如趁年末，為自己的神學路向「充充電」？
不少朋友都曾表示，在修讀神學之前，最想了解的是「老師是怎樣的？」、「神學院的環境如何？」——不妨親身來到崇基神學院看看，不必帶著一堆疑問自行猜測！
當晚你可參與由本院神學生負責的週四崇拜，崇拜後將有時間與老師一對一傾談，亦可藉此機會認識本院的同學，親身感受這裡的氛圍與氣息。
活動費用全免，並會提供簡便晚餐，請放心赴會！
無論你剛開始思考、仍有猶豫，或已帶著一堆問題想發問——我們都歡迎你前來坐坐，與我們聊聊。
出席老師：葉漢浩教授、白德培教授 (Prof. Tobias Brandner)、溫誠敦教授 (Prof. Bruce Worthington)、朱安之教授、駱頴佳博士、姚志豪牧師、邵倩文副校牧
日期：2026年10月29日（四）晚上6時至9時
地點：香港中文大學崇基學院容啟東校長紀念樓G樓聖堂
截止報名：2026年10月23日（五）
（
如今次未能出席，下一場將於明年3月舉行，敬請留意我們稍後的公佈！）
網上報名 ：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13743164
招生詳情：
https://www.theology.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions
"Meet and Greet" Thursday Gathering
As autumn deepens, why not use this end-of-year moment to "recharge" your theological journey?
Many friends have shared that before studying theology, what they most want to know is: "What are the teachers like?" and "What's the atmosphere at the Divinity School of Chung Chi College?" — why not come see for yourself, instead of guessing with a head full of questions!
That evening, you're welcome to join the Thursday Service led by our Theology students. After the service, there'll be time for one-on-one conversations with our teachers, as well as a chance to meet fellow students and experience the atmosphere here firsthand.
The event is completely free, and a light dinner will be provided — so come with an easy heart!
Whether you're just starting to consider this path, still have some hesitations, or already have a long list of questions — you're warmly invited to come, sit with us, and have a chat.
Teachers joining us: Prof. Ip Hon-ho Alex, Rev. Prof. Tobias Brandner, Prof. Bruce Worthington, Prof. Gillian Chu, Dr. Lok Wing-kai Peter, Rev. Yiu Chi-ho, and Miss Vicky Shiu.
Date: Thursday, 29 October 2026, 6:00 – 9:00pm
Venue: Divinity School Chapel, G/F, President Chi-tung Yung Memorial Building, Chung Chi College, CUHK
Registration deadline: Friday, 23 October 2026
(
If you can't make it this time, our next session will be held in March next year — stay tuned for more details!)
Register online：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13743164
Admissions information：
https://www.theology.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Divinity School of Chung Chi College

title: [Taster Event] Greater Bay Area Day Trip with IBCE and ABS - Transfer-in Business Programmes (6 November)
bodyText:
Mass Mail System

2026/10/09
»
Announcements
[Taster Event] Greater Bay Area Day Trip with IBCE and ABS - Transfer-in Business Programmes (6 November)  - Global Business Programmes, CUHK Business School
From: Global Business Programmes
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
denniswong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear first-year students,
Ready to transform your university experience and stand out in today’s competitive business landscape?
The
International Business and Chinese Enterprise (IBCE)
and
Asian Business Studies (ABS)
transfer-in programmes are designed to cultivate regional expertise across diverse business contexts, while developing career readiness, professional networks, and focused skill sets.
To experience firsthand how IBCE and ABS can help you achieve your goals, we invite you to join our exclusive taster event - the
Greater Bay Area Day Trip on 6 November
!
As a core part of our professional training, the day trip is designed to enhance students’ regional business exposure. You will visit the thriving Greater Bay Area, a key driver of China’s technological advancement and economic growth, and bridge classroom knowledge with real-world business strategy.
Event Highlights
Go behind the scenes at two Chinese technology companies:
Sunwoda Electronic Co Ltd and UBTECH Robotics
to understand the latest developments in lithium-ion batteries and robotics
Gain strategic insights through interactive sessions with senior executives
Learn how these companies navigate and lead within Asia’s complex business landscape
Meet our Programme Director and current IBCE/ABS students to learn about the programme experience
Event Details
Date
: 6 November 2026 (Friday)
Time
: 08:30 – 18:00
Meeting Point
: Futian Port
Itinerary
: Visit Sunwoda Electronic Co Ltd (AM) and UBTECH Robotics (PM)
Cost
: Free of charge
Transportation
: Shuttle bus service will be provided within Shenzhen. Participants are responsible for their own transportation between Hong Kong and Shenzhen.
Lunch
: Self-arranged at your own expense
Important Note
: Check the validity of your travel document and renew it if needed. Verify visa requirements for China and make your own arrangements in advance, if necessary.
Spaces are limited. To secure your spot, please complete this
webform
by 25 October
. Successful applicants will receive a confirmation email before the event.
We look forward to sharing a rewarding learning experience with you!
Should you have any questions, please feel free to contact Mr. Dennis Wong at
denniswong@cuhk.edu.hk
or 3943 7643.
Best regards,
Dennis Wong
Programme Manager
Global Business Programmes
Undergraduate Office
CUHK Business School

4/F, Cheng Yu Tung Building, 12 Chak Cheung Street, Shatin, Hong Kong

Dear all,
We cordially invite you to attend our upcoming
International Summit on Pain Research -
A CUHK and CUHK-Shenzhen Joint Forum
on
15 October 2026 (Thursday)
at Lecture Theatre 2, G/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA).
Featuring renowned speakers from the US, UK and Mainland China, the forum will delve into circuit mapping, neural mechanisms, and novel therapeutic opportunities in pain research.
In addition, emerging young researchers will share their latest findings and showcase cutting-edge translational research spanning microglial priming, hydrogel brain interfaces, and VR pain therapies.

title: CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC  - Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre
From: Yolanda YIM
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yolandayim@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
An Opportunity to Conduct Research in A
rctic Regions
_________________________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in the
17th
Chinese National Arctic
Research Expedition 2027
.
Research opportunities are available at
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2, Yellow River Station
and
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
in Arctic Regions. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2
Quota:
Tentatively 1-2 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Shanghai aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in June or July 2027
Return to Shanghai in Sep or Oct 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Shanghai
Yellow River Station
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Longyearbyen to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Longyearbyen and from Hong Kong
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Akureyri and drive to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights from Hong Kong to Reykjavík, onward travel to Akureyri, and ground transportation to the station.
Priority consideration:
Applicants with existing research collaborations or academic connections in Iceland
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
April-May
for loading and transportation to the Arctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain a Schengen visa for Yellow River Station or CIAO
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Accommodation on the stations before and after station entry/exit or during the expedition in the stations
(Accommodation on Xuelong or Xuelong 2 is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
10 November 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Arctic Regions and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

From: The Graduate School Office

[Invitation] Graduate School Seminar 202
6
: “
AI in Education
”
As
CUHK Graduate School
celebrates its
60th Anniversary
, we are not only reflecting on six decades of excellence, innovation, and impact, but also looking ahead to the future of education in an increasingly AI-driven world.
To mark this milestone, we are pleased to invite you to join us on 6 November 2026 (Fri) for a series of celebration activities
,
including our annual signature event, the
Graduate School Seminar 202
6:
“
AI in Education
”
, a
networking session
bringing together speakers, students, and alumni from diverse backgrounds and disciplines, as well as a
mini exhibition
showcasing the Graduate School’s history and achievements.
Jointly organised by the CUHK Graduate School and the Federation of Graduate School Alumni Associations (FGSAA), the
Graduate School Seminar 2026: "AI in Education"
presents a forward-looking dialogue on how artificial intelligence is transforming teaching and learning, research, and graduate education.
We are honoured to welcome three distinguished speakers who will share their insights on the evolving role of AI in education in keynote speeches and panel discussion:

"From Knowledge to Discovery: AI and the Future of Graduate Education"
Professor Irwin KING
- Pro-Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President (Education)
- Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Keynote Speaker & Panelist

"How Hong Kong Education City can Assist in the Implementation of the
Blueprint for Digital Education Development in Primary and Secondary Schools
"
Mr. Armstrong LEE
- Chairman, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK MBA
Keynote Speaker

"Standardised AI Literacy and Certification: Lessons from Southeast Asia"
Dr. Winson WONG
- Certified AI Trainer of United Nations University
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Keynote Speaker & Panelist
Dr. Tenny LAM
- Executive Director, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Panelist
Moderator:
Prof. Anthony SO, Dean of the Graduate School
Drawing on their diverse expertise across academia, education, and industry, our speakers will share insights on the opportunities and challenges presented by AI technologies, and discuss their implications for the future of higher education.
The Seminar will conclude with a
networking session with refreshments
, providing an opportunity for alumni, students, academics, and professionals to connect, exchange ideas, and explore new collaborations.

Date:
6 November 2026 (Friday)

Time:
15:00  – 17:30

Venue:
VR Zone, Learning Garden, LG/F, University Library, CUHK
Shuttle bus service will be provided between University MTR Station and the CUHK University Library according to the designated schedule
Online Registration:
Please click
here
to register online via CUHK Registration and Attendance System on or before 23 October 2026 (Friday).
All CUHK, CUHK(SZ) and CUSCS students, alumni and staff are welcome to sign up for the event.
Join us as we celebrate 60 years of excellence and reimagine the future of graduate education at CUHK and beyond.

18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者
廣東話為母語
使用智慧型手機並可持續連接互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策

18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策

使用指定的訊息應用程式

Invitation to ICS Public Lecture – Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee on 15 October 2026 誠邀參加中國文化研究所訪問學人公開講座──李晉美博士（芝加哥藝術學院） - Institute of Chinese Studies
From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 15 October 2026. It is our honour to welcome Dr. Jennifer Dorothy LEE, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, to deliver a talk on the topic:
“Shuttered Eyes, Kinship Threads: Tracing Music and Migration in the Family of Yo-Yo Ma”
.
Abstract:
What can a single photograph say? The black-and-white artefact featured in this talk, a product of the Nanjing Guanghua Photo Studio, shows a family like many others in 1946, caught between wars and continents. The figures pictured are musicians, primarily, but also teachers, scientists, and jacks-of-all-trades. They are the progenitors of the famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, of his sister Yeou-Cheng, and of me. Drawing on lenses that range from music to art history to something akin to critical fabulation, I unfold the episodic, recursive process of unearthing my family history for the very first time. The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,

From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 29 October 2026. It is our honour to welcome Prof. Ping WANG, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from Department of Asian Languages and Literature at the University of Washington, to deliver a talk on the topic: "Untranslating the Poet-Transcendent: Li Bo (701–762) Between Cosmology and Equivalence".
Abstract:
Large language models now translate between languages in seconds, reviving an old anxiety: is translation a solved problem? This talk argues that for understanding a culture, fluency was never the difficulty. Taking the great Tang poet Li Bo as its case, it follows a singularly iconic word, xian 仙, the term behind his epithet "poet-transcendent," as it passes into English. In medieval China, a xian was not merely a being who does not die; a xian held rank and office in a celestial bureaucracy, and could be demoted from it. To render Li Bo a "banished immortal" keeps the exile but quietly drops that cosmic officialdom, leaving behind a familiar romantic genius. For a century "immortal" was the dominant English choice, canonized in dictionaries and anthologies until it seemed self-evident. Machine translation, trained on that same archive, reproduces the reduction as its frictionless default, laying bare how thoroughly it saturated the record. The question, then, is not whether cultures can be translated, but how a concept, precisely by resisting translation, becomes a shared medium for thinking transcendence.
Speaker:
Ping Wang is Professor in the Department of Asian Languages and Literature at the University of Washington, where she teaches classical Chinese literature and researches the history of Chinese poetry. She has previously held faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin and Princeton University, prior to joining the University of Washington.
Professor Wang's scholarship bridges Western sinology, translation studies, traditional Chinese classical learning, and contemporary critical theory. She has published numerous articles and is the author of
The Age of Courtly Writing: Wen xuan Compiler Xiao Tong (501-531) and His Circle
and
The Poetic Way of Xie Lingyun
, the latter of which examines the significance of landscape poetry (shanshui shi) in Chinese literary history.
Her honors include a research membership at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, a special Andrew W. Mellon Foundation grant for international collaborative research, and a research fellowship from the Simpson Center for the Humanities at the University of Washington. In 2017, she was invited to lecture at the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia, and she is currently a resident fellow of the Institute of Chinese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Invitation to Translation Talks @ CUHK #3: Ecotranslation for the Sake of Environmental Education  - Department of Translation
From: Katie Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
katiecheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Department of Translation is pleased to invite you to the third session of our
Translation Talks @ CUHK
series:
Ecotranslation for the Sake of Environmental Education
Speaker:
Prof. Darryl Cameron Sterk
Affiliation:
Lingnan University

Date:
23 October 2026 (Friday)

Time:
12:30 p.m.

Venue:
Room 214, Li Dak Sum Building, CUHK
In this engaging talk, Prof. Sterk will explore how translation can contribute to environmental education and biodiversity awareness. Drawing on examples from bilingual digital databases, visual media, and emerging AI applications, he will discuss how ecotranslators, educators, scientists, and policymakers work together to make knowledge about nature more accessible to the public.
This lecture offers a unique opportunity to discover the intersections between translation, ecology, technology, and education, while reflecting on how language can help foster a deeper understanding of the natural world.
About the Speaker
Prof. Darryl Cameron Sterk is an Associate Professor of Translation at Lingnan University, Hong Kong. His research focuses on the role of translation in minority language revitalization, particularly in the era of digital communication and technological innovation.

Registration:
Please register via the QR code on the poster or through the registration link provided.
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/T66DURZtLz
We warmly welcome all students, staff, researchers, and members of the public who are interested in translation studies, environmental communication, and interdisciplinary research.
We look forward to seeing you at the talk.

For non-tonal language speakers What's the difference between mā and má? Get 400 HKD to discover !！-Month2  - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: CAI Penghao
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
penghaocai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Can you hear the difference between mā and má? How does your brain learn language tones? Join our study and put your ears to the test!
In our study, you will attend two sessions:
In the first session (EEG), you will wear a comfortable sensor cap so we can record your brain activity while you listen to sounds. (Safe & Non-invasive!)
In the second session (Behavioral), you will conduct interactive computer-based tasks that test your focus and memory.
NO
prior experience with Mandarin or Cantonese is required — we welcome everyone as long as you are eligible!
Location: the Chinese University of Hong Kong
What You’ll Get
A unique opportunity to see how your brain works
Learn something new about tones and language learning
$400 compensation for your time
If you’re interested, sign up here:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScisZwrnju0zMkecXd0vFTyBS03moME0Ix8uVxSJSwEzFeMLw/viewform

We will contact you later to schedule an experiment with you if you are eligible.
Eligibility
:
Aged 18–30; NOT majoring in psychology or linguistics.
Be a non-tonal language native speaker (e.g. non-Mandarin/non-Cantonese).
Normal hearing and vision.
No history of brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological conditions; no scalp injuries or infections.
Right-handed, healthy, no hair dyeing within two weeks before the experiment.
For inquiries, please contact:
penghaocai@cuhk.edu.hk

Join us at “Study in Europe Fair” at YIA on Friday, 23 October!

The third edition of the
Study in Europe Fair
will take place on Friday, 23 October! The event is proudly organised by the European Union Office to Hong Kong and Macao in cooperation with Consulates-General of EU Member States and The Chinese University of Hong Kong. It is a must-attend event for all Hong Kong students interested in pursuing an academic exchange or a degree programme in Europe.
Three highlights of the event:
12 EU countries showcasing a wide range of study and exchange opportunities for undergraduates and postgraduates students from Hong Kong, including scholarships
Discover the EU's flagship Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programmes and scholarship opportunities
Chat with local alumni and hear about their unique study experiences in Europe!

Want to gain real research experience while supporting a meaningful project for Hong Kong’s business community in the digital age?

We are now recruiting part-time student helpers to support our survey and interview activities.

講者 Speaker: 門泊舟博士 Dr. MEN Bozhou
主持 Moderator: 蔣元秋博士 Dr. JIANG Yuanqiu
日期 Date: 16 / 10 / 2026 (Fri)
時間 Time: 4 p.m. - 6 p.m.
地點 Venue: 香港中文大學 大學書店（康本國際學術園一樓） University Bookstore (YIA 1/F), CUHK
普通話主講 In Putonghua
簡介 Synopsis
當奧德修斯重返伊塔卡，珀涅羅珀二十年的等待終得回報。但好奇的讀者或許也曾有一閃念：如果珀涅羅珀沒有選擇等待呢？本講座通過文學中的對照手法，看看荷馬是否在《奧德賽》中留下一些線索來回答這個問題。我們也會討論：女性命運抉擇的背後，究竟牽扯到怎樣激烈的政治交鋒和殘酷的時代印記。

Wish to transform your R&D results to a real business and become an entrepreneur?
If you wish to turn your research output into a real business, please consider applying for the
Technology Startup Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU)
. Or, if your students wish to commercialize their R&D results, please also encourage them to apply for TSSSU.
Successful applicants may receive
Up to HK$600,000 funding per year for potentially up to three years
Potential to join HKSTP’s Incubation Programme
Access to potential investors & industry partners
Mentorship from experienced entrepreneurship consultant
Apply Now IF
Your idea is innovative, your team is capable, your innovation and technology are unique and your business plan is sound
Your team wants to make a societal impact and is passionate about entrepreneurship
Eligibility of a PIC
The Person-in-Charge (PIC) of a CUHK TSSSU company must be a full-time CUHK student, a full-time CUHK professor, or alumni graduated within the last three years.
Compulsory Requirements:
For TSSSU-O & TSSSU+ applications, preference will be given to those who are
entitled to exploit technology owned or licensed from CUHK
(excluding those technology developed from InnoHK Centres incorporated by CUHK)*.
The technology involved in the application must reach the required Technology Readiness Level (TRL).
Physical Science and Engineering technology must reach TRL 4 or above
and
HealthCare technology must reach TRL 3 or above
.
The number of members of the Company must be
at least two
including the eligible PIC. Active members of CUHK should be the effective majority of shareholders of the Company.
Fulfill all the eligibility requirements in CUHK TSSSU Guideline 202
7
-2
8
.
(TSSSU+ only) The assessment panel shall review the investment arrangement during the assessment process per the request of ITC.  Please submit the
agreement
issued by the private investor together with the applications.  If the agreement has not yet been signed, please submit the latest available draft agreement.
* If a patent application has not been filed at the time of submission of a TSSSU-O or TSSSU+ application, the applicant should consider submitting an Invention Disclosure Form or a Copyright Disclosure Form and Assignment to the KTO IP and Technology Licensing Team.

MPSS -
LivingWorks safeTALK (English)
Dear Students,
Do you want to support your friends, classmates, or anyone in need? Join us for LivingWorks safeTALK, a four-hour, internationally recognized training that equips people to be more alert to someone thinking of suicide and better able to connect them with further help.
Through this workshop, you will learn the simple and practical TALK model:
Tell: Tell someone directly that you’re concerned
Ask: Ask clearly and openly about suicide
Listen; Listen with empathy and without judgment
KeepSafe: Keep the person safe by connecting them to appropriate resources

Dear Students,
To strengthen non-local students' resilience and equip students to cope with life’s challenges, sign up for the 12-hour Mental Health First Aid Standard Course taught by qualified counsellors who are certified MHFA trainers by The Mental Health Association of Hong Kong.
Upon completion of the course, participants will be able to:
Identify the signs and symptoms of common mental health and substance use challenges;
Provide someone with initial support until they are connected with appropriate professional help;
Identify risk factors and warning signs for mental health and addiction concerns; and
Learn strategies to help someone in both crisis and non-crisis situations, and know where to turn for help.

Voices of the CU-riosities
Starting from zero to build a book house in Africa — How?
"We hope this building gives Kibera's children a place to play, learn, and belong, it can show the world and the next generation of architects that design has the power to change lives," said Associate Professor Peter Winston Ferretto, Director of the School of Architecture at CUHK, who led the project, summing up his and his students' aspiration in a few words.
The project is called the Amani Kibera Book House. "Amani" means peace in Swahili, and Kibera is one of Africa's largest informal settlements. It is a place facing intense economic struggles, where nearly a million people live under extreme conditions and official municipal infrastructure is scarce. Before Professor Ferretto and his team arrived, nobody could imagine the possibility of a public space where children could play and learn, locals could gather and dance, and women could work and earn.

Lab to Society | Monthly Pulse (October 2026)
Voices of the CU-riosities
Starting from zero to build a book house in Africa — How?
"We hope this building gives Kibera's children a place to play, learn, and belong, it can show the world and the next generation of architects that design has the power to change lives," said Associate Professor Peter Winston Ferretto, Director of the School of Architecture at CUHK, who led the project, summing up his and his students' aspiration in a few words.
The project is called the Amani Kibera Book House. "Amani" means peace in Swahili, and Kibera is one of Africa's largest informal settlements. It is a place facing intense economic struggles, where nearly a million people live under extreme conditions and official municipal infrastructure is scarce. Before Professor Ferretto and his team arrived, nobody could imagine the possibility of a public space where children could play and learn, locals could gather and dance, and women could work and earn.

---------------------------------------------------
Dear students,
The collaborative study between CUHK and UST is recruiting the last batch of participants! If you are interested, please enrol in this study now!
We are inviting undergraduate students to take part in a study exploring the relationship between emotion and learning experience. If you are (1)
over 18 years old
, (2) are an
undergraduate student
, (3) have
lived in Hong Kong for at least 3 years
, and (4) can
read Traditional Chinese and speak Cantonese fluently
, please read on!
INCENTIVES
If you can complete Part 1, Part 3, Part 4 and at least 80% of the daily surveys in Part 2 for this study, you will receive HKD$300 supermarket e-coupon.
WHAT TO DO?
Part 1: Please complete a 15-minute survey now:
https://ust.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cFGMgIN5ZBDU3jM
Upon the completion of Part 1, you can download or update surveyYIK (iOS ver. 1.4.2 & Android ver. 1.4.1.97).
Part 2: Starting tomorrow (till 31 Dec), we will send you a notification each evening at 8pm during which you will complete a short survey
before midnight
.
Part 3: In early Jan 2027, you will complete a 30-minute survey.
Part 4: In late Jan 2027, you will complete another 10-minute survey.
Please contact Jasmine via email at
happyu@ust.hk
or WhatsApp at 2358-5050 if you have any questions.
Note
:
Please ignore this email if you have completed the survey through previous recruitments. No extra compensation will be distributed to repeated participants
.
Best regards,
Jasmine Wong
HKUST Emotion and Personality Research Group

Click the link below to register and complete an initial questionnaire (approx. 10 minutes).

[16 Oct Anthropology Friday Seminar] Anne-Christine Trémon, "Regrets of the future. Critiques of unfulfilled promises and fake urbanization in Shenzhen."  - Anthropology
From: M.W.Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
anthropology@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear all,
You are cordially invited to join a talk on 16 October, in which Prof. Anne-Christine Trémon will discuss inhabitants' critique of urban transformation in urbanized villages in Shenzhen, China.
Title: Regrets of the future. Critiques of unfulfilled promises and fake urbanization in Shenzhen.
Speaker: Anne-Christine Trémon (School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (EHESS))
Date: Friday 16 October, 2026
Time: 1:00-2:30pm
Mode: In-person
Venue: Room 114, Humanities Building, New Asia College, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Abstract:
In Shenzhen as elsewhere in China the effects of the country's dramatic real estate crisis have unleashed changes that were striking amid my revisit to the field after years of absence. In this talk, I analyse the critical discourse I encountered regarding not only failed real estate projects, but also urban transformation itself. Among the inhabitants of urbanized villages in Shenzhen's periphery, the prevailing mood has shifted from optimism during my earlier field work to pessimism, and even outspoken resentment. Comparing the situation before and after the crisis allows pinpointing precisely where their shift in attitude lies. It also allows highlighting that critical discourse is not limited to moral outrage. People do not simply blame unfulfilled promises, they expose the fakeness of urbanisation policies, which they no longer view as a motor for growth and progress toward the future. Overall, I argue that inhabitants' critique is related to their no longer being in sync with urbanization: to their simultaneous feeling of stagnation and being out of step with the present.

We all know group projects can be... challenging. What if you had an
AI project manager
that breaks down tasks, writes meeting notes, and helps resolve disagreements?
Use Copilot
to keep your team on track and your project drama-free.
Prompt 1 — copy & paste it!
Break it down
"Our group project is: [describe]. We have 4 members and 3 weeks. Break into specific tasks with: 1) Clear deliverables per person 2) Dependencies 3) Deadlines 4) A risk and mitigation plan."
Prompt 2 — keep the conversation going!
Meeting minutes in seconds
"Here are rough notes from our group meeting: [paste notes]. Turn these into professional minutes with: attendees, key decisions, action items (who/what/when), and next meeting items."
Prompt 3 — go advanced!
Resolve disagreements
"Our team disagrees on [issue]. Person A thinks [A] and Person B thinks [B]. Give an objective pros/cons analysis, then suggest a compromise taking the best of both."
Why this works:
Copilot is the neutral third party every group project needs. No sides, no drama, just clear action plans!

Bonus tip:
Before final submission:
"Review our project for consistency in writing style, formatting, and tone — make it sound like one person wrote it"

for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

title: Simply Pocket Oasis Workshop 「靜系」掌心水苔球工作坊
bodyText:

Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
Simply Pocket Oasis Workshop 「靜系」掌心水苔球工作坊 - Shaw College
From: Jessie LI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jessieli@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Every day, you're busy creating PowerPoint slides, essays, reports and CVs...
But when was the last time you created a moment of inner peace for yourself?
Join us to design and craft your own miniature Zen garden, and give yourself a moment to simply be. Through your five senses, reconnect with yourself and the present moment, while letting your body and mind truly rest.
Come and create your pocket oasis!
Date: 31 October 2026 (Sat)
Time: 10:00 - 12:00
Venue: LG501, Wen Lan Tang, Shaw College, CUHK
Quota: 24
Target: CUHK Students, Staff, Alumni and the General Public (Priorities are given to Friends of the Arts members and CUHK Undergraduate Students)
Fee: Please refer to the application form
Online Application:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742389
Application Deadline: 16 October 2026 (Fri)
Enquiry: Ms. Chow (
florachow@cuhk.edu.hk/
3943 1549)
我們每天都在創造很多東西——PowerPoint、Essay、報告、CV…
卻很少創造一刻真正屬於自己的平靜。
這一次，用雙手打造一個掌心盆景，留下一段與自己同行的時間。
透過五感覺察，與自己和當下連結，
一邊設計並製作屬於你的掌心盆景，一邊讓身心好好休息。
快來打造你專屬的「掌心心靈綠洲」吧！
日期: 2026年10月31日 (星期六)
時間: 10:00 - 12:00
地點: 香港中文大學逸夫書院文瀾堂LG501
名額: 24人
對象: 中大學生、教職員、校友及公眾人士 (Friends of the Arts 會員及中大本科生優先)
費用: 請參考報名表
網上報名︰

florachow@cuhk.edu.hk

Gerald Choa Neuroscience Institute (GCNI) is now looking for student helpers for GCNI Symposium 30 November & 1 December 2026. Details are listed below:
Date:
30 November & 1 December 2026 (Monday & Tuesday)
Time:
8:15 am - 5:30 pm (Day 1), 9:15 - 1:00 (Day 2)
Venue:
YIA LT2
Duties:
Counter reception, poster design, IT support, logistics coordination, taking photos etc.
Hourly rate:
HK$64/hour
(Free lunch and refreshments will be provided)
Application link and deadline:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13743990
On or before 23 October 2026
Remarks:
A paid 2-hour briefing session will be held on 29 November 2026 (Sunday).
Only full time CUHK students are eligible to apply.
You must register for Student Helper Engagement Scheme before the event if appointed.
Non-local students must present your “No Objection Letter” issued by the Immigration Department.
Preference will be given to applicants available for the briefing session on 29 Nov, the whole session on 30 Nov (08:15 - 17:30) and the whole session on 1 Dec (09:15 - 13:00).
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and receive our confirmation email after the application deadline.

bodyText:

From: Dorothy Yuen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cuoaa@cuhk.edu.hk

禪繞 X 瑪雅印記初探
找回真正的自己快樂做自己
瑪雅印記是什麼？中美洲古瑪雅文明的智慧，說著每個人出生時都有與生俱來的『天賦才華』。此課程將引領你找到『它』，用另一角度認識自己，運用在你的生活/人際關係//工作/家庭中。
「一筆一畫，無限可能。」禪繞是一場筆與紙的自我對話，發現更多未知的自己。不需任何繪畫技巧，沒有對與錯，沒有美與醜，只需筆隨心轉，一筆一畫，療癒心靈，放鬆地繪出自己的世界。
禪繞畫是一種簡單而自由的繪畫技巧，易於入門，可以幫助人們學會專注和集中注意力，並激發創造力和想像力。這些因素都使得禪繞畫成為一種非常適合作為藝術入門的繪畫技巧。
它們都是友善的工具，讓你們禪繞遇見<我的瑪雅, 我的天賦>。

bodyText:

Announcements
Mindfulness Workshop: Connect Your Body, Mind & Nature Certificate Upon Completion of All Four Sessions 【正念工作坊】連結身心與自然｜完成四節可獲出席證書 - Department of Educational Administration and Policy
From: WONG Hoi Yan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155219686@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

心身連結正念工作坊
本工作坊旨在協助參加者學習正念的態度與技巧，連結當下的身心狀態，增進對韌性（resilience）及自然為本療癒概念的理解，並透過五感體驗與大自然建立更深的連結。

日期及時間
• 正念基礎：2026年11月3日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 覺察情緒：2026年11月10日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 智慧的心：2026年11月17日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
• 連結世界：2026年11月24日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

地點
香港中文大學校園（崇基校園），活動將於戶外及室內場地進行。

語言
以廣東話為主，英語輔助。

重要事項
• 每位學生嚮導最少須參加兩節正念體驗工作坊。 • 首兩節工作坊為必須出席，參加者必須出席：
2026年11月3日：正念基礎
2026年11月10日：覺察情緒
能夠出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲優先考慮。
出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲發出席證書 
由於部分活動將於戶外進行，參加者請穿著舒適、適合戶外活動的衣物及鞋履
本活動由香港中文大學教育學院 PDTL Grant 贊助。

計畫負責人及導師
劉雅詩博士
註冊中學教師
香港中文大學教育行政與政策學系高級講師
自2007年起致力向職前教師及在職教師推廣靜觀（正念）。

查詢
李小姐：
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
成功報名的參加者將獲電郵通知。
報名連結：
https://forms.gle/YLKv4soaARwBHkgF8

Mindfulness & Body-Mind Connection Workshop
This workshop aims to help participants cultivate mindfulness attitudes and skills, develop a deeper connection with the present moment and their body-mind experience, and enhance their understanding of resilience and nature-based healing. Through experiential activities involving the five senses, participants will also have the opportunity to build a closer connection with nature.

Dates and Times
• Mindfulness Foundations: 3 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • Cultivating Emotional Awareness: 10 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • The Wisdom of the Heart: 17 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. • Connecting with the World: 24 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

Venue
The Chinese University of Hong Kong campus, Chung Chi Campus. The workshop will take place in a combination of outdoor and indoor settings.

Language
Primarily Cantonese, with English support.

Important Notes
• Each student guide is required to attend at least two mindfulness experiential workshop sessions. • The first two sessions are mandatory. Participants must attend:
3 November 2026: Mindfulness Foundations
10 November 2026: Cultivating Emotional Awareness
• Priority will be given to students who are able to attend all four sessions.
• Students who attend all four workshop sessions will receive an attendance certificate 
• As some activities will be conducted outdoors, participants are advised to wear comfortable clothing and suitable footwear for outdoor activities 
This activity is sponsored by the PDTL Grant of the Faculty of Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Course Trainer
Dr. Lau Ngar Sze
Registered Secondary School Teacher
Senior Lecturer, Department of Educational Administration and Policy,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. Lau has been promoting mindfulness among pre-service and in-service teachers since 2007.

Enquiries
Miss Fiona Li:
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
Successful applicants will be notified by email.
Registration link

本工作坊旨在協助參加者學習正念的態度與技巧，連結當下的身心狀態，增進對韌性（resilience）及自然為本療癒概念的理解，並透過五感體驗與大自然建立更深的連結。

日期及時間
• 正念基礎：2026年11月3日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 覺察情緒：2026年11月10日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 智慧的心：2026年11月17日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
• 連結世界：2026年11月24日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

地點
香港中文大學校園（崇基校園），活動將於戶外及室內場地進行。

語言
以廣東話為主，英語輔助。

重要事項
• 每位學生嚮導最少須參加兩節正念體驗工作坊。 • 首兩節工作坊為必須出席，參加者必須出席：
2026年11月3日：正念基礎
2026年11月10日：覺察情緒
能夠出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲優先考慮。
出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲發出席證書 
由於部分活動將於戶外進行，參加者請穿著舒適、適合戶外活動的衣物及鞋履
本活動由香港中文大學教育學院 PDTL Grant 贊助。

計畫負責人及導師
劉雅詩博士
註冊中學教師
香港中文大學教育行政與政策學系高級講師
自2007年起致力向職前教師及在職教師推廣靜觀（正念）。

chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk

https://forms.gle/YLKv4soaARwBHkgF8

Mindfulness & Body-Mind Connection Workshop
This workshop aims to help participants cultivate mindfulness attitudes and skills, develop a deeper connection with the present moment and their body-mind experience, and enhance their understanding of resilience and nature-based healing. Through experiential activities involving the five senses, participants will also have the opportunity to build a closer connection with nature.

Dates and Times
• Mindfulness Foundations: 3 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • Cultivating Emotional Awareness: 10 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • The Wisdom of the Heart: 17 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. • Connecting with the World: 24 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

Venue
The Chinese University of Hong Kong campus, Chung Chi Campus. The workshop will take place in a combination of outdoor and indoor settings.

Language
Primarily Cantonese, with English support.

Important Notes
• Each student guide is required to attend at least two mindfulness experiential workshop sessions. • The first two sessions are mandatory. Participants must attend:
3 November 2026: Mindfulness Foundations
10 November 2026: Cultivating Emotional Awareness
• Priority will be given to students who are able to attend all four sessions.
• Students who attend all four workshop sessions will receive an attendance certificate 
• As some activities will be conducted outdoors, participants are advised to wear comfortable clothing and suitable footwear for outdoor activities 
This activity is sponsored by the PDTL Grant of the Faculty of Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Course Trainer
Dr. Lau Ngar Sze
Registered Secondary School Teacher
Senior Lecturer, Department of Educational Administration and Policy,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. Lau has been promoting mindfulness among pre-service and in-service teachers since 2007.

社區藥房提供的服務

藥劑師如何成為您可靠的社區健康夥伴

Sharing by HIA Community Pharmacy: Understanding Community Pharmacy Services

Free Health Check for Chronic Disease
Have you ever wondered how pharmacists can support your health beyond dispensing medicines?
Join us for an informative sharing session by a pharmacist from
Health In Action (HIA) Community Pharmacy
and learn how community pharmacy services can support you and your family in maintaining good health.

Date:
16 October 2026 (Friday)

Time:
2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Venue:
Activity Room 1–3, Quarryside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay

Language:
English

Speaker:
Pharmacist from Health In Action Community Pharmacy

Quota:
20 participants
⭐⭐⭐
Free health check for blood pressure, blood glucose and cholesterol will be available after the talk!!
‼⭐
What will you learn?
The role of pharmacists in primary healthcare
Services provided by community pharmacies
Safe use of medications and medication management
Support available for minor ailments and chronic disease management
How pharmacists can become your trusted community health partners
Health In Action believes that community pharmacies can serve as an important first point of contact for healthcare services. Through health education, medication management, and community-based pharmacy services, pharmacists play an important role in helping individuals and families stay healthy and informed.
This session is suitable for members of multicultural communities, community workers, caregivers, and anyone interested in learning more about healthcare services in Hong Kong.

Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3QnJthMMwdTKD2K
Places are limited and will be allocated on a
first-come, first-served basis
. Successful registrants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation message.

Successfully registered participants who attend the event will receive a special souvenir!
‼⭐
We look forward to seeing you and exploring how pharmacists can support healthier communities together!
JCSATH

齊來認識腸道健康 Trust Your Gut: From Early Life to Everyday Wellbeing 免費健康篩查驗三高   - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

TRUST YOUR GUT
齊來認識腸道健康
免費健康篩查驗三高
您知道嗎？腸道的功能不僅僅是消化食物！腸道微生物群（Gut Microbiome）對我們的身體健康、心理健康、免疫力、睡眠質素以及整體生活質素都擔當著重要角色。研究顯示，我們的飲食習慣、睡眠質素、運動量，甚至壓力水平，都會影響腸道健康。
誠邀您參加這個內容豐富且實用的健康講座，一同了解如何透過簡單的生活習慣，促進腸道健康，提升整體身心健康。
認識什麼是腸道微生物群，以及它如何在生命早期建立
了解腸道健康、免疫系統及心理健康之間的關係
認識微生物群研究的方法，以及您如何參與相關研究
了解睡眠、運動、飲食及壓力如何影響腸道健康
獲取維持健康生活方式的實用貼士
無論您希望改善個人健康、關注家人的身心健康，還是單純對腸道健康感興趣，都歡迎參加！

日期：
2026年10月16日（星期五）
⏰
時間：
中午12:00 至 下午1:00

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海善里 20 號）

名額：
20人

語言：
英語（設有廣東話及南亞語言傳譯服務）
⭐⭐⭐完成健康講座後設有免費健康篩查, 量度血壓、血糖、膽固醇
!
‼⭐

歡迎家長攜同子女一同參加。

報名連結
：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eIZxGg6CKyBC9ts

查詢
：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
一齊了解日常生活中的小習慣，如何為腸道健康帶來大改變，提升整體身心健康！
成功登記及出席將獲贈精美紀念品乙份‼⭐
Trust Your Gut: Health Talk Free Health Check for Chronic Disease
Did you know that your gut does much more than digest food? The gut microbiome plays an important role in our physical health, mental wellbeing, immunity, sleep, and overall quality of life. Research shows that what we eat, how we sleep, how active we are, and even our stress levels can influence our gut health.
Join us for an informative and practical health talk to learn how simple lifestyle choices can support a healthier gut and improve overall wellbeing.
Learn what the gut microbiome is and how it is established in early life

title: 超越現實的畫作：藝術 × 混合實境（Mixed Reality）體驗
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
超越現實的畫作：藝術 × 混合實境（Mixed Reality）體驗   - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

超越現實的畫作：藝術
×
混合實境（
Mixed Reality
）體驗

誠邀你參加一個結合藝術同混合實境（MR）科技嘅創意工作坊，與來自不同文化背景的朋友一同創作一幅屬於大家的立體藝術作品，共同描繪香港故事。
參加者將透過 MR 技術在同一個實體及虛擬空間進行 3D 繪畫，分享自己對香港的回憶、感受、生活點滴和想法。你可以自由創作、與其他參加者合作，或者在之前參加者的作品上加入新元素。隨著創作慢慢累積，一幅集合不同文化背景、不同生活經歷的大型立體藝術作品將會逐步形成。
體驗嶄新混合實境（MR）科技
在沉浸式空間進行 3D 創作
用藝術分享你眼中的香港
與不同文化背景的參加者互動交流
無需任何藝術或科技經驗
歡迎所有文化背景人士參加。
即使你不想親身創作，都歡迎以觀賞者身份參與，透過觀賞專用頭戴裝置欣賞創作過程，以及不斷演變的立體藝術作品。

日期：
2026年10月15日（星期四）
⏰
時間：
下午2:00 至 5:30

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside  舍區 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海善里 20 號）

名額：
20位參加者

語言
:
英語為主 (現場設有廣東話及南亞語言翻譯)
一齊探索藝術和科技如何促進跨文化交流，透過創作認識彼此，從不同角度重新欣賞香港！

報名連結：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0TGkqUSP8Dc5WqW

報名截止日期：
2026年10月11日（星期日）

查詢：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
注意事項
• 名額有限，先到先得。
• 成功報名者將於活動最少2日前收到 WhatsApp 確認通知。如未收到確認訊息，則表示未能成功獲得名額。
無需
任何繪畫技巧或科技知識，只要帶住你的好奇心、創意，和屬於你的香港故事一同參與！

=====================================================================

Drawing Beyond Reality: Art & MR Experience

What does Hong Kong look like through your eyes?
Join us for a unique
Mixed Reality (MR) art workshop
where people from different cultural backgrounds come together to create a shared
3D artwork
about life in Hong Kong.
Using
MR technology
, participants will draw and create in the
same physical and virtual space
, expressing their memories, experiences, feelings, and perspectives of Hong Kong. You may create your own artwork, collaborate with others, or add to drawings created by previous participants. Together, we will build a collective 3D artwork that reflects the
diverse stories
and voices of our community.
Experience Mixed Reality technology
Create artwork in a 3D immersive space
Explore memories, experiences, hopes, and everyday life in Hong Kong
No art or technology experience required
Participate as a creator or observer
We welcome participants from all cultural backgrounds, including
members from multicultural communities
and Chinese communities.
Even if you do not wish to create artwork yourself, you can still join as an observer and explore the evolving virtual artwork through dedicated observation headsets.

Date:
15 October 2026 (Thursday)
⏰
Time:
2:00 PM - 5:30 PM

Venue:
Quarryside

Quota:
20 registered participants

Language:
English (interpretation available in Cantonese and South Asian languages)
Come and explore how art and technology can bring people together, spark conversations, and help us see Hong Kong through one another's eyes.
Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0TGkqUSP8Dc5WqW
Registration Deadline: 11 October 2026 (Sunday)
Enquiries: JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
Notes
• Due to limited places, registration is on a first-come, first-served basis.
• Successful registrants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation at least 2 days before the event. If you do not receive a confirmation message, your registration is considered unsuccessful.
Open to people from all cultural backgrounds. Let's explore our stories, communities, and experiences together through creativity and technology.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Master of Social Science in Sustainable Tourism (MSSST) Programme, Department of Geography and Resource Management
The Department of Geography and Resource Management (GRM) at CUHK has long been at the forefront of sustainability education, research, and practice at local, regional, and global levels. Established in 2007, the MSSST Programme is a pioneering and distinctive postgraduate programme that advances sustainable tourism through interdisciplinary education, experiential learning, research-informed practice, and engagement with industry, government, and communities. Building on its strengths in sustainable tourism, resource management, tourism governance, and destination development, the Programme continues to evolve in response to emerging challenges and opportunities in Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area, China, and beyond.
Join a vibrant learning community committed to creating positive change through tourism. Through innovative and experiential learning, the Programme develops responsible sustainable tourism leaders equipped with the knowledge, professional skills, and ethical values to contribute to industry innovation, community wellbeing, and a more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient future.
You are welcomed to register via the link above. Should you have any questions, please feel free to email us at MSSST@cuhk.edu.hk.

Format: Zoom

Master of Science in GeoInformation Science and Smart Cities
This programme is designed for graduates from a range of disciplines, specifically for graduates who have completed an undergraduate degree in geography, ecology, environmental science, surveying, civil engineering, urban planning, GIS or remote sensing, or practitioners or officers/officials in the similar fields who seek to develop a career or improve their careers in relation to applied GIS/remote sensing technologies. This programme aims at providing students with a solid conceptual framework and technical know-how by enhancing their skills and equipping them with hands-on experience. It also introduces the state-of-the-art geo-spatial information technologies and provides students with the capability to manage and apply the latest technologies to solve real life problems. In recent years, the trend of smart cities development (i.e., urban areas that use different types of electronic methods and sensors to collect data in improving the operations across the city) has been getting apparently important, while geoinformation science is the major tool for materializing the concept of smart cities.

Announcements
Recruitment of Student Internship 招募實習學生 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Edwin Chung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
shunkitchung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院研究團隊現正進行一項
社區研究。本計劃透過免費提供空氣清新機，幫助居住在空氣質素欠佳環境
的 6 至 17 歲哮喘兒童及青少年改善居住環境。
我們誠邀中大本科生加入參與實習，
一同走進社區，透過科學方法協助家庭。
工作範疇
- 研究期間：即日起至 2027 年 10 月 31 日（按團隊編排彈性參與）
- 協助研究團隊在指定的日期和地點進行研究對象招募。
- 按日子到研究對象的住所設置空氣監測儀器、放置空氣清新機，並為研究對象進行呼吸測試。
- 執行研究團隊指派的其他工作。
招募條件
- 現正就讀大學學士學位課程的學生（醫學、護理、公共衛生或相關課
程更佳）。
- 具備良好溝通技巧，能操流利廣東話（具適量普通話水平更佳）。
- 熟悉基本電腦應用。
報名方式
如有興趣參與本研究實習，請將個人履歷傳送至電郵：jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
（郵件標題請註明：申請哮喘兒童研究學生實習)
聯絡及查詢
香港中文大學賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院
負責同事: Sang/Edwin
電話：(852) 2252 8744
電郵：jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
The research team from the Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
is currently conducting a community study. This project aims to improve the living conditions of children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 with asthma who reside in poor air quality environments by providing them with free air purifiers.
We sincerely invite CUHK undergraduate students to join us as interns to step into the community and assist these families through scientific methods.
Scope of Work
Research Period:
From now until October 31, 2027 (flexible participation based on the team's schedule)
Participant Recruitment: Assist the research team in recruiting study subjects at designated dates and locations.
Home Visits & Testing: Visit the subjects' homes to set up air monitoring equipment, place air purifiers, and conduct respiratory tests for the subjects.
Other Duties:
Execute other tasks assigned by the research team.
Recruitment Criteria
Education:
Current undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor's degree (preferably in Medicine, Nursing, Public Health, or related programs).
Languages:
Good communication skills, fluent in Cantonese (proficiency in Mandarin is a plus).
Skills:
Familiar with basic computer applications.
Application Method
If you are interested in participating in this research internship, please send your resume to jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
(Please use the subject line: Application for Pediatric Asthma Study Student Internship
).
Contact and Inquiries
Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
Contact Persons:
Sang / Edwin
Phone:
(852) 2252 8744
Email:
jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Subject: 研究資助局公眾講座 - 兒童發展、學習與家庭介入(Research Grants Council Public Lectures to be conducted in Cantonese)
香港高等院校進行了很多令人振奮的學術研究計劃。為了讓市民更了解本地研究的重要性及價值，研究資助局定期舉辦公眾講座，向大眾分享最新研究成果。
研資局將於今年﹙2026﹚舉辦一系列與STEAM教育相關的公眾講座，講題包括人工智能與文物保育、網上訂價、兒童教育及宇宙探索。這些講座旨在提升市民對相關方面最新研究成果的認識。講座詳細內容如下：講座以粵語進行。免費入場，座位先到先得，有興趣人士亦可於網上收看講座現場直播或稍後重温。詳細內容如下：(
https://www.ugc.edu.hk/big5/rgc/about/events/lectures/lectures.html
)
The Hong Kong higher education sector has undertaken many exciting academic research projects. To raise public awareness of the significance and values of the local research work, the Research Grants Council regularly organises public lectures to share the latest research results with the public.
This year (2026), the RGC has organised a series of public lectures related to STEAM education, covering topics including cultural preservation with artificial intelligence, online pricing, children education, and universe exploration (conducted in Cantonese). These lectures aim to enhance the awareness of the latest researches in related areas. Please refer to Chinese version for more details.

When their village is devastated and their family is forced to flee, siblings

bodyText:

[Webinar] Understanding Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) [網上講座]認識多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症 (多囊卵巢綜合症) - The Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology (O&G)
From: Cynthia Lai
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sukhanlai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
今年5月，醫學界將多囊卵巢綜合症（Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, PCOS）重新命名為多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症(Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome, PMOS)，因為它不僅是婦科問題，還涉及內分泌和代謝失調。香港中文大學醫學院的研究更指出，PMOS 不僅影響患者本人，還可能增加下一代在心臟健康、代謝、生殖及糖尿病方面的風險，顯示此症對女性及家庭健康有深遠影響。
為了讓大眾更深入了解，本中心將舉行「認識多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症 (多囊卵巢綜合症)」網上講座，誠邀大眾參與，一同掌握最新資訊。講座詳情如下：
日期： 10 月 26 日 (星期一)
時間： 下午 5:30 – 6:30
平台： Zoom（廣東話進行）
費用：全免，歡迎所有人士參與
主持： 鍾佩樺醫生
講者： 馬青雲醫生、張麗冰醫生、吳逸晞博士
報名：立即掃描海報上的 QR code 或擊點
https://forms.gle/PGVPd42VcXTxHGc8A
查詢電話：3505 1456
Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) has been renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) this May, as medical experts have recognized that it is not only a gynecological condition but also involves endocrine and metabolic disorders. Research from The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)’s Faculty of Medicine (CU Medicine) further indicates that PMOS affects not only patients themselves but may also increase risks for the next generation in areas such as heart health, metabolism, reproduction, and diabetes—highlighting its profound impact on women’s and family health.
To help the public gain deeper understanding, our center will host an online seminar: “Understanding Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome)” We warmly invite everyone to join and stay informed with the latest updates.
Date: October 26 (Monday)
Time: 5:30 PM – 6:30 PM
Platform: Zoom (conducted in Cantonese)
Fee: Free of charge, open to all
Moderator: Doctor Chung Pui Wah Jacqueline
Speakers: Doctor Ma Ching Wan Ronald, Doctor Cheung Lai Ping, Dr. Ng Yat Hey Noel

From: Horatio Gong

The Department of Social Work is delighted to share that the Research Programme for Aging and Disabilities has invited
Prof. Nathan Boucher
, Associate Professor of Public Policy, Nursing, and Medicine at Duke University, to offer a research seminar on “Community Engagement as a Public Policy Imperative in Caregiving Research”. This seminar will be held in hybrid mode (in-person & Zoom).
We warmly invite you to attend the seminar. For details, please find in the attached poster and below:
Time: 4 November 2026 (Wednesday); 2:30 p.m.-4:00 p.m.
Speaker: Prof. Nathan Boucher, Associate Professor of Public Policy, Nursing, and Medicine at Duke University
Venue: Room 520, Chen Kou Bun Building, CUHK (
Google Maps
) & Zoom
Registration: Please register via
this link
or scan the QR code in the poster
About the Seminar: Community engagement is essential to relevant and equitable aging and caregiving research. Dr. Nathan Boucher argues that lived experience should be treated as a form of data and incorporated throughout the research lifecycle. Older adults, family caregivers, clinicians, community organizations, and system leaders can help identify meaningful outcomes, expose structural inequities, and reveal contextual factors that administrative and clinical datasets often miss. Partnership-driven approaches—including interviews, focus groups, advisory councils, listening sessions, and user-centered design—can improve construct validity, feasibility, implementation, and policy translation. Community engagement also reduces research waste by aligning questions and interventions with the priorities of those most affected. Examples from aging, Veterans’ health, homelessness, and the direct care workforce illustrate how engagement can refine research questions, identify unintended consequences, and generate more responsive practices and policies. The presentation concludes that investing in engagement infrastructure is not optional; it is fundamental to producing sustainable, legitimate, and meaningful health systems research.
About the Speaker: Nathan Boucher is an expert in assessing patient and caregiver experiences during serious illness. As a Research Scientist with US Veterans Administration Health Systems Research and Associate Professor at Duke University, he specializes in both qualitative and intervention research at the intersection of social care and healthcare for older populations in need. Dr. Boucher leads projects to support family caregivers and older adults—including those assisting older adults re-entering the community from prison—and develops innovative interventions for families living with dementia and other serious illness. Dr. Boucher’s multidisciplinary perspective bridges clinical practice, health/social policy, and community engagement to drive meaningful advances in health and social supports for older adults.
Should you have any enquiries, please feel free to contact Mr. Horatio Gong at 39431709 or
horatiogong@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you very much.

From: Horatio Gong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

The Department of Social Work is delighted to share that the Youth and Childhood Research Programme and the Family and Group Practice Research Programme has invited
Prof. Christopher Wretman
, Associate Professor/Senior Lecturer in Quantitative Research Methods at School of Social and Political Science, The University of Edinburgh, to offer a research seminar on “Current Approaches to Child Abuse Response in Scotland: The “Child’s House” Model”
We warmly invite you to attend the seminar. For details, please find the attached poster and below:
Time: 2:00pm-3:30pm, 16 October 2026 (Friday)
Speaker: Prof. Christopher Wretman, Associate Professor/Senior Lecturer in Quantitative Research Methods, School of Social and Political Science, The University of Edinburgh
Venue: Room 509, T. C. Cheng Building, CUHK (
Google Maps
)
Registration: Please register via
this link
or scan the QR code in the poster
About the Seminar: Since about 2021, Scotland has been implementing a series of interventions translated as “Child’s House” that seek to transform the coordination of service delivery in cases of child abuse. This work is driven by the following key question: "What happens to a child after they report/disclose abuse?" And, as a follow-up: “How can stakeholders make this process better for children and their families?" Realizing that traditional responses are often varied across police, health, education, and social work settings, and can feel traumatic and draining, “Child’s House” has been adapted in Scotland from a European model with a focus on co-located, multi-disciplinary, and inter-agency service delivery that hopes to simplify and improve child abuse response. “Child’s House” offers a shared spaced where different service provides can work together to deliver services to address children's rights to safety, justice, and recovery. An experienced team at the University of Edinburgh is leading efforts to promote and evaluate “Child’s House” in Scotland with a vision for changing how children experience services after abuse.
This lecture will cover four points. First, a discussion of current child abuse response legislation and policy frameworks in Scotland. Second, an overview of the “Child’s House” intervention model. Third, an overview of the University of Edinburgh team’s ongoing evaluation approaches. Fourth, and finally, preliminary findings and implications for global approaches to child protection.
Should you have any enquiries, please feel free to contact Mr. Horatio Gong at 3943 1709 or
horatiogong@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you very much.

https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx

- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html

協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/TC/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx
